issues.legal_issue: A report originating solely in conciliation proceedings is confidential and cannot be introduced as evidence in judicial proceedings, even if it does not fall within the specific categories listed for exclusion.
material_facts: A demarcation report was prepared by a government agency in the course of conciliation proceedings.
The report’s genesis was solely in the conciliation proceedings, and recourse to those proceedings was necessary to establish its origin.
A party sought to introduce the report as evidence in judicial proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The report could not be admitted into evidence. The judgment admitting it was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 75 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 requires the conciliator and parties to keep confidential all matters relating to conciliation proceedings; the expression “relating to” has wide import, as recognised in Renusagar Power Company Limited v. General Electric Company. Applying the test in Ruby General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pearey Lal Kumar, a matter relates to a proceeding where recourse to that proceeding is necessary to determine the matter in dispute. Section 81’s listed categories do not limit the broader confidentiality obligation in Section 75. The Court distinguished Union Carbide Canada Inc. v. Bombardier Inc., which recognises that evidence of a fact independent of and separate from a settlement offer may be used.

predicates.judicial_proceeding_seeks_report_as_evid: A party sought to introduce a report as evidence in a judicial proceeding.
predicates.report_originated_only_in_conciliation: The report was generated solely in the course of conciliation proceedings.
predicates.determining_report_origin_requires_recou: Establishing the report’s origin required recourse to the conciliation proceedings.

issues.definition: When a judicial proceeding seeks a report as evidence and the report originated only in conciliation, with its origin ascertainable only by recourse to conciliation, the report is inadmissible.

issues.legal_issue: Evidence of a fact independent of and separate from conciliation may be introduced in judicial proceedings in accordance with the ordinary rules of admissibility.
material_facts: The report at issue originated solely in conciliation proceedings.
The party seeking to rely on it could obtain another report from authorities for the purpose of demarcating the property.
issues.conclusion: The party remained free to obtain an independent report from authorities and seek to introduce it in evidence in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court agreed with Union Carbide Canada Inc. v. Bombardier Inc. that a litigant cannot object to evidence of a fact independent of and separate from a settlement offer. It distinguished the report at issue because that report originated solely in conciliation, while leaving open the introduction of an independently obtained report in accordance with law.

predicates.judicial_proceeding_seeks_demarcation_ev: A party seeks to present evidence about the demarcation of property in a judicial proceeding.
predicates.report_obtained_independently_of_concili: The report was obtained from authorities independently of the conciliation proceedings.

issues.definition: When demarcation evidence is sought in a judicial proceeding and the report was obtained independently of conciliation, the report may be introduced in accordance with law.
